overview.summary: LLMGateway is a single-process local service that intercepts developer queries, classifies their complexity, routes them to the most appropriate backend, and returns the response. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP interface so existing tooling requires no changes. All state is local; no cloud dependency is required for operation.

subsystems.name: Ingress
subsystems.purpose: Accepts incoming queries and normalises them to an internal format.

subsystems.name: Routing
subsystems.purpose: Classifies queries and selects the appropriate backend.

subsystems.name: Backend Execution
subsystems.purpose: Dispatches queries to configured backends and collects responses.

subsystems.name: Observability
subsystems.purpose: Records query history and routing decisions for developer inspection.

subsystems.name: Configuration
subsystems.purpose: Loads and validates user-supplied backend configuration at startup.

components.name: API Server
components.purpose: Exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP interface and translates requests into internal query objects.
responsibilities: Accept HTTP requests on the configured port.
Validate and parse incoming request payloads.
Translate OpenAI-format requests to internal Query objects.
Return responses in OpenAI-compatible format.
Enforce request size limits.

components.name: Query Classifier
components.purpose: Assigns a complexity tier to each query to inform routing decisions.
responsibilities: Analyse query content and estimate complexity.
Assign a tier label (e.g. simple, moderate, complex) to each query.
Operate within a bounded latency budget to avoid adding routing overhead.

components.name: Router
components.purpose: Selects the appropriate backend for a query based on classification, availability, and configured priority.
responsibilities: Receive classified queries and select a backend.
Respect user-configured backend priority order.
Detect unavailable backends and trigger fallback.
Pass explicit backend overrides through without reclassification.

components.name: Backend Pool
components.purpose: Maintains the registry of configured backends and their current availability status.
responsibilities: Store the list of configured backends and their metadata.
Track availability state of each backend.
Expose backend selection interface to the Router.
Perform periodic health checks on configured backends.

components.name: Local Backend Adapter
components.purpose: Dispatches queries to locally-running LLM backends such as llama.cpp or LM Studio.
responsibilities: Translate internal Query objects to the local backend's native format.
Send requests and receive responses from local backends.
Report backend errors to the Router for fallback handling.

components.name: Cloud Backend Adapter
components.purpose: Dispatches queries to remote cloud LLM APIs such as OpenRouter or Anthropic.
responsibilities: Translate internal Query objects to the target cloud API format.
Manage API key injection for cloud requests.
Handle cloud-specific rate limiting and retry logic.
Report backend errors to the Router for fallback handling.

components.name: Query Log
components.purpose: Persists a record of each query, routing decision, backend used, and response latency.
responsibilities: Write a structured log entry for every completed query.
Expose a query history read interface for developer inspection.
Enforce log retention limits to prevent unbounded disk growth.

components.name: Config Loader
components.purpose: Loads, validates, and hot-reloads user-supplied backend configuration from disk.
responsibilities: Parse configuration file from disk at startup.
Validate configuration structure and required fields.
Expose validated configuration to other components.
Watch for configuration file changes and reload without restart.

dataModel.notes: All entities (Query, Backend, RouteDecision, LogEntry) are defined in the DataSpec. The architecture treats them as immutable value objects passed between components — no component mutates another component's entity.

apiContract.authStrategy: Local Unix socket or localhost-only HTTP — no authentication required for single-user local deployment. API key injection for cloud backends is handled internally by the Cloud Adapter and is never exposed to the caller.
apiContract.notes: The external interface is intentionally OpenAI-compatible so that existing tools (Continue, Aider, OpenCode) require no reconfiguration.

dataFlow.name: Query Routing Flow
dataFlow.description: The primary path a developer query takes from ingress to response.

steps.action: Receives HTTP request and parses it into a Query object.
Assigns a complexity tier to the Query.
Selects the appropriate backend based on tier and availability.
Dispatches Query to the selected local backend and awaits response.
steps.notes: If selected backend is cloud, cloud-adapter handles this step instead.

steps.action: Writes a log entry with backend used, latency, and outcome.
Returns response to the caller in OpenAI-compatible format.

dataFlow.name: Backend Fallback Flow
dataFlow.description: How the system recovers when the preferred backend is unavailable.

steps.action: Detects backend failure response from adapter.
Marks failing backend as unavailable and returns next candidate.
Retries routing with next available backend.

dataFlow.name: Configuration Load Flow
dataFlow.description: How backend configuration reaches the components that need it.

steps.action: Reads and validates configuration file from disk at startup.
Receives validated backend list and initialises availability state.
Reads backend priority order from backend-pool.

constraints.description: The gateway must run as a single process on a single machine with no external service dependencies required for local-only operation.
constraints.rationale: Developer tooling must work offline and in air-gapped environments.
constraints.name: Authentication Required

constraints.description: The external API interface must be OpenAI-compatible so that existing developer tools require no reconfiguration.
constraints.rationale: Adoption requires zero friction for developers already using OpenAI-compatible clients.
constraints.name: Rate Limiting

constraints.description: All routing logic must complete within the NFR-001 overhead budget and must not block the response path with I/O.
constraints.rationale: Routing overhead must be imperceptible to the developer.
constraints.name: Data Encryption

constraints.description: No component may directly access another component's internal state — all interaction is through defined interfaces.
constraints.rationale: Enforces component boundaries and makes the system testable in isolation.
constraints.name: Input Validation
